subject: Triggered growth credit mechanism — proposal and next steps
body:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Anika Rao <anika@heliosai.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Triggered growth credit mechanism — initial proposal

Hi Anika —

Thanks again for the time this morning. As discussed, we put together a short proposal to address Helios' mid-contract growth risk while keeping unit economics predictable on both sides. The high-level idea is a triggered credit that unlocks when actual monthly usage exceeds forecasted baseline by certain thresholds; credits can be redeemed against the next invoice or applied as committed top-up capacity.

Key points:
- Trigger thresholds: +20% and +50% vs. the baseline forecast (monthly).
- Credit allocation: 50% of the incremental token spend above baseline between +20% and +50%; 75% credit for incremental spend > +50% (applied pro-rata).
- Vesting: credits accrue monthly and vest over 3 months (i.e., credit becomes redeemable across the following three billing cycles).
- Prepay incentive: if Helios prepays for 3 months of committed capacity up-front, we can add a one-time 10% bonus credit applied to the first billing cycle after cutover.
- Co-term: any purchased top-up capacity will co-term to the annual contract end; no separate billing contract.

Attached: Helios_PRICING_COMPARISON.xlsx (shows modeled spend scenarios) and a draft of the top-up terms.

Ask: can you share the most recent monthly baseline forecast (or typical +/- swing) so we can validate thresholds? If that looks reasonable, I can route this to our pricing team and send a finalized amendment + DocuSign.

Cheers,
Connor O'Brien

From: Anika Rao <anika@heliosai.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:12:27 -0800
Subject: Re: Triggered growth credit mechanism — initial proposal

Connor —

Appreciate the thoughtful structure. A few quick clarifying questions from our side:
1) How does the credit interact with overage pricing? If we hit the +50% bucket and get the 75% credit, do we still pay the full overage and then receive a credit back, or are we billed net of credits immediately?
2) What are the rollback protections if our forecast drops? We have seasonal spikes (Q1) and then dips; we can't take on credits that expire instantly.
3) Any impact to SLAs/priority for burst capacity if we take advantage of this program? Helios needs guaranteed burst capacity for model retrains.

Also, procurement asked whether credits could be used to offset a short-term committed prepay if we decide to go that route. I can pull in our procurement lead if needed.

Thanks,
Anika Rao
Director of Platform Ops | Helios AI
anika@heliosai.com

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>

Cc: Anika Rao <anika@heliosai.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 08:18:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Triggered growth credit mechanism — initial proposal

Team —

Fwd'ing Anika's questions and the original proposal. We need pricing/legal guidance on the following quick points so we can respond by EOD Friday:
- Credit settlement: Anika asked whether the credit is netted at billing time or paid as a refund. My preference is net billing (credits applied to the invoice to avoid cash refunds). Any constraints?
- Vesting mechanics: I suggested a 3-month vesting window to avoid gaming / sudden forecast drops. Would marketing accept 3 months or prefer a different decay?
- SLA implications: Helios requires burst capacity guarantees for retrains — can we commit to a burst runway with a soft priority (best-effort) vs. hard SLA? If we add burst SLAs, that affects pricing.

Notes for context: Helios' finance team is conservative on credits but responsive if there's a prepay bonus. They asked specifically about using credits to offset a prepay.

Thanks —
Connor

---

On Thu, Dec 3, 2026 at 08:35 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:

Connor / team,

Good notes. My recommendations (quick):
1) Billing: credits are applied net at invoice time. Keep refunds off the table to simplify accounting. Language: "Credits will be applied against future invoices; cash refunds will not be issued."
2) Vesting / decay: make credits accrue monthly but expire after 9 months with a linear decay after month 3 (so full credit available months 1–3, then 75% month 4–6, 50% month 7–8, 25% month 9). That protects Redwood while giving Helios runway.
3) Prepay: we can offer the 10% bonus only if they prepay at least 3 months of committed capacity; bonus is applied once and does not roll into future renewals. Allow credits to offset a short-term prepay (yes) — but limit use to 50% of prepay amount to prevent circularity.
4) Burst capacity: offer a "Burst Priority Lite" add-on — guarantees burst capacity subject to regional availability and defined throttles (no hard latency SLA). If Helios wants a hard SLA for retrains, that needs to be quoted separately as a Dedicated capacity uplift.

I'll attach a slightly cleaned terms doc with the decay schedule.

Marissa Cole
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Final proposal: Triggered credit + prepay incentive (summary & next steps)

Anika —

Thanks for the follow-ups and for sharing procurement's initial concerns. Based on internal guidance, here's the consolidated proposal for Helios: 

Summary (finalized):
- Triggers: +20% and +50% vs. agreed baseline. Baseline = 3-month rolling forecast agreed in writing.
- Credits: 50% of incremental spend between +20% and +50%; 75% of incremental spend above +50%.
- Vesting & decay: credits accrue monthly and are fully redeemable months 1–3; 75% redeemable months 4–6; 50% months 7–8; 25% month 9; credits expire after month 9.
- Prepay incentive: 10% one-time bonus when Helios prepays >= 3 months of committed capacity. Bonus cannot exceed 50% of the prepay value when combined with credits.
- Billing: credits netted at invoice time (no cash refunds). Credits can offset up to 50% of a short-term prepay if Helios chooses that path.
- Burst capacity: Offer "Burst Priority Lite" as an add-on (no hard SLA). If Helios needs hard retrain SLAs, we will price Dedicated uplift separately.
- Co-term: any top-up capacity purchased will co-term with the existing annual contract end date.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm you are okay with the vesting/decay schedule and whether the baseline (3-month rolling forecast) is acceptable.
2) If yes, I'll send an amendment via DocuSign for signature. Link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/ZZ-HELIOS-8842
3) I'll create a HubSpot task and attach the signed amendment; sales ops will schedule billing sync for the prepay if you elect that option. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/DEAL-8842

If procurement wants to jump on a quick 20-minute call tomorrow to finalize language around credit accounting, happy to join.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
